newsitem.title: FRANCE: France rejects pro-French militants in Comoros.
newsitem.headline: France rejects pro-French militants in Comoros.

text.p: France on Wednesday denounced secessionists demanding independence for the Indian Ocean island of Anjouan in the Comoros archipelago or a return to the French fold.

"France respects the integrity of states and notably the integrity of the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros...and condemns separatist initiatives there," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
Authorities imposed a curfew on the island on Tuesday after clashes between security forces and youths protesting against the arrest of a pro-secessionist leader.

Sporadic gunfire was heard as demonstrators armed with petrol bombs set up roadblocks of burning tyres and battled security forces who fired teargas, according to witnesses. Several people were reported wounded.
Rummelhardt said Paris also deplored the events of July 14, when three people were killed in similar clashes.
"The situation is serious and can potentially de-stabilise the region," he said.
Tuesday's fighting followed a government decision last week to outlaw two main pro-secessionist parties.
The Comoro Islands have a population of 190,000 and became independent from France in 1975, except for the island of Mayotte, which chose to remain French.
Many residents of Anjouan, the second largest island, say independence has brought only poverty, civil strife and numerous coups.
The main leader of a pro-secessionist movement, Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, 75, and another leader, Charikane Ahmed, were transferred to the main island, Grande Comore, on Tuesday under heavy guard.

Ibrahim was arrested late on Monday after being called by three government emissaries to the office of newly appointed Anjouan Governor Cheikh Allaoui for a meeting. Family members said he had been lured into a trap.
Several people were also killed in clashes in March.
